diff --git a/snapback4/crates/snapback4-lang/tests/wave12_semantics.rs b/snapback4/crates/snapback4-lang/tests/wave12_semantics.rs
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..a589ba9349
--- /dev/null
+++ b/snapback4/crates/snapback4-lang/tests/wave12_semantics.rs
@@ -0,0 +1,381 @@
+use snapback4_core::{Context, Engine, Value, WriteState};
+use snapback4_lang::{compile, types::Ty};
+use std::collections::BTreeMap;
+
+fn checked(source: &str) -> snapback4_lang::Bound {
+    let bound = compile(&[("schema.q".into(), source.into())]);
+    assert!(bound.diagnostics.is_empty(), "{:#?}", bound.diagnostics);
+    bound
+}
+
+fn engine(source: &str) -> Engine {
+    let bound = checked(source);
+    Engine::memory(bound.schema, bound.programs.into_iter().map(|program| program.program)).unwrap()
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn global_count_is_zero_then_tracks_inserts_and_deletes() {
+    let source = r#"
+table entries:
+  public
+  insert <- allow
+  delete <- allow
+  online only
+table moderators:
+  principal: principal
+  unique principal
+  read <- .principal = viewer
+  online only
+view total: count entries
+  read <- allow
+  online only
+view privateTotal: count entries
+  read <- exists moderators[viewer]
+  online only
+mutation add(id: id):
+  return insert entries { id }
+mutation remove(id: entries):
+  delete entries[id]
+  return null
+query totalEntries():
+  return total
+query privateEntries():
+  return privateTotal
+"#;
+    let bound = checked(source);
+    let generated = snapback4_lang::emit::typescript(&bound);
+    let native = snapback4_lang::emit::rust::rust(&bound);
+    assert!(!generated.contains("$global") && !native.contains("$global"),
+        "the physical discriminator leaked into generated application types");
+    for expression in ["total first 1 by .id", "total[true]"] {
+        let bound = compile(&[("bad.q".into(), format!("{source}\nquery bad(c: cursor ?):\n  return {expression}\n"))]);
+        assert!(bound.diagnostics.iter().any(|diagnostic| diagnostic.code == "E_QUARRY_TYPE"
+            && diagnostic.message.contains("global maintained scalar")), "{expression}: {:#?}", bound.diagnostics);
+    }
+    let mut engine = engine(source);
+    let query = |engine: &mut Engine| engine.query("totalEntries", Context::new("alice", BTreeMap::new())).unwrap().data;
+    let private = |engine: &mut Engine, viewer| engine.query("privateEntries", Context::new(viewer, BTreeMap::new())).unwrap().data;
+    assert_eq!(query(&mut engine), Value::Int(0));
+    assert_eq!(private(&mut engine, "alice"), Value::Null, "an unauthorized empty global stays hidden");
+    engine.seed([("moderators".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([
+        ("id", Value::Id("mod".into())), ("principal", Value::Id("alice".into())),
+    ]))]).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(private(&mut engine, "alice"), Value::Int(0), "authorized absence is the count identity");
+    assert_eq!(private(&mut engine, "bob"), Value::Null, "a hidden absence is not zero");
+    for id in ["a", "b"] {
+        let outcome = engine.mutate("add", None, Context::new("alice", BTreeMap::from([("id".into(), Value::Id(id.into()))]))).unwrap();
+        assert!(matches!(outcome.state, WriteState::Sent { .. }), "{outcome:?}");
+    }
+    assert_eq!(query(&mut engine), Value::Int(2));
+    assert_eq!(private(&mut engine, "alice"), Value::Int(2));
+    assert_eq!(private(&mut engine, "bob"), Value::Null, "a hidden stored scalar remains null");
+    engine.mutate("remove", None, Context::new("alice", BTreeMap::from([("id".into(), Value::Id("a".into()))]))).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(query(&mut engine), Value::Int(1));
+    engine.mutate("remove", None, Context::new("alice", BTreeMap::from([("id".into(), Value::Id("b".into()))]))).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(query(&mut engine), Value::Int(0));
+    assert!(engine.store().rows("total").unwrap().is_empty(), "zero deletes the physical aggregate row");
+    assert!(engine.store().rows("privateTotal").unwrap().is_empty(), "private zero also has no physical row");
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn matching_count_guard_narrows_only_the_same_required_projection_until_a_write() {
+    let schema = r#"
+table entries:
+  owner: principal
+  score: int
+  optionalScore: int ?
+  by byOwner: owner, id
+  public
+  insert <- allow
+  delete <- allow
+  online only
+"#;
+    let sound = checked(&format!(r#"{schema}
+query stats(owner: principal):
+  n = count(entries[owner] by byOwner)
+  require n > 0 else EMPTY
+  return {{ low: min(entries[owner] by byOwner, .score), high: max(entries[owner] by byOwner, .score), total: sum(entries[owner] by byOwner, .score) }}
+query filtered(owner: principal):
+  require count(entries where .owner = owner) > 0 else EMPTY
+  return min(entries where .owner = owner, .score) + 1
+mutation freshAfterWrite(owner: principal, victim: entries):
+  delete entries[victim]
+  n = count(entries[owner] by byOwner)
+  require n > 0 else EMPTY
+  return min(entries[owner] by byOwner, .score) + 1
+"#));
+    let result = &sound.programs.iter().find(|program| program.program.name == "stats").unwrap().result;
+    assert!(matches!(result, Ty::Object(fields) if fields.values().all(|ty| ty == &Ty::Int)), "{result:?}");
+    assert_eq!(sound.programs.iter().find(|program| program.program.name == "filtered").unwrap().result, Ty::Int);
+
+    for (name, body) in [
+        ("different", "n = count(entries[owner] by byOwner)\n  require n > 0 else EMPTY\n  return min(entries['other'] by byOwner, .score) + 1"),
+        ("optional", "n = count(entries[owner] by byOwner)\n  require n > 0 else EMPTY\n  return min(entries[owner] by byOwner, .optionalScore) + 1"),
+        ("written", "n = count(entries[owner] by byOwner)\n  require n > 0 else EMPTY\n  delete entries[victim]\n  return min(entries[owner] by byOwner, .score) + 1"),
+        ("stale_binding", "n = count(entries[owner] by byOwner)\n  delete entries[victim]\n  require n > 0 else EMPTY\n  return min(entries[owner] by byOwner, .score) + 1"),
+        ("rebound", "n = count(entries[owner] by byOwner)\n  n = 1\n  require n > 0 else EMPTY\n  return min(entries[owner] by byOwner, .score) + 1"),
+        ("joined", "n = count(entries[owner] by byOwner)\n  if flag:\n    n = 1\n  require n > 0 else EMPTY\n  return min(entries[owner] by byOwner, .score) + 1"),
+        ("root_rebound", "who = owner\n  n = count(entries[who] by byOwner)\n  who = next\n  require n > 0 else EMPTY\n  return min(entries[who] by byOwner, .score) + 1"),
+    ] {
+        let args = match name {
+            "written" | "stale_binding" => "owner: principal, victim: entries",
+            "joined" => "owner: principal, flag: bool",
+            "root_rebound" => "owner: principal, next: principal",
+            _ => "owner: principal",
+        };
+        let kind = if matches!(name, "written" | "stale_binding") { "mutation" } else { "query" };
+        let bound = compile(&[("schema.q".into(), format!("{schema}{kind} {name}({args}):\n  {body}\n"))]);
+        assert!(bound.diagnostics.iter().any(|d| d.code == "E_QUARRY_TYPE" && d.message.contains("int ?")), "{name}: {:#?}", bound.diagnostics);
+    }
+
+    let helper = compile(&[("schema.q".into(), format!(r#"{schema}
+fn remove(victim: entries):
+  delete entries[victim]
+  return true
+mutation staleHelper(owner: principal, victim: entries):
+  n = count(entries[owner] by byOwner)
+  removed = remove(victim)
+  require n > 0 else EMPTY
+  return min(entries[owner] by byOwner, .score) + 1
+"#))]);
+    assert!(helper.diagnostics.iter().any(|d| d.code == "E_QUARRY_TYPE" && d.message.contains("int ?")), "{:#?}", helper.diagnostics);
+
+    let authority = compile(&[("schema.q".into(), format!(r#"{schema}
+job staleAuthority():
+  for row in entries:
+    n = count(entries[row.owner] by byOwner)
+    as row.owner:
+      require n > 0 else EMPTY
+      narrowed = min(entries[row.owner] by byOwner, .score) + 1
+"#))]);
+    assert!(authority.diagnostics.iter().any(|d| d.code == "E_QUARRY_TYPE" && d.message.contains("int ?")), "{:#?}", authority.diagnostics);
+
+    let self_dependent = compile(&[("schema.q".into(), r#"
+table buckets:
+  bucket: int
+  score: int
+  by byBucket: bucket, id
+  public
+  online only
+query staleSelfDependent():
+  bucket = 1
+  bucket = count(buckets[bucket] by byBucket)
+  require bucket > 0 else EMPTY
+  return min(buckets[bucket] by byBucket, .score) + 1
+"#.into())]);
+    assert!(self_dependent.diagnostics.iter().any(|d| d.code == "E_QUARRY_TYPE" && d.message.contains("int ?")),
+        "a count result must not inherit the old value's domain provenance: {:#?}", self_dependent.diagnostics);
+
+    let pure_domain = checked(&format!(r#"{schema}
+fn sameOwner(owner: principal):
+  return owner
+query pureDomain(owner: principal):
+  n = count(entries[sameOwner(owner)] by byOwner)
+  require n > 0 else EMPTY
+  return min(entries[sameOwner(owner)] by byOwner, .score) + 1
+"#));
+    assert_eq!(pure_domain.programs.iter().find(|program| program.program.name == "pureDomain").unwrap().result, Ty::Int);
+
+    let impure_domain = compile(&[("schema.q".into(), format!(r#"{schema}
+fn changingOwner(owner: principal, victim: entries):
+  delete entries[victim]
+  return owner
+mutation staleDomain(owner: principal, victim: entries):
+  n = count(entries[changingOwner(owner, victim)] by byOwner)
+  require n > 0 else EMPTY
+  return min(entries[changingOwner(owner, victim)] by byOwner, .score) + 1
+"#))]);
+    assert!(impure_domain.diagnostics.iter().any(|d| d.code == "E_QUARRY_TYPE" && d.message.contains("int ?")),
+        "writeful domains must never be replayed as aggregate proof: {:#?}", impure_domain.diagnostics);
+
+    let shadowed = compile(&[("schema.q".into(), format!(r#"{schema}
+fn count(owner: principal):
+  return 1
+query shadowedCount(owner: principal):
+  n = count(owner)
+  require n > 0 else EMPTY
+  return min(entries[owner] by byOwner, .score) + 1
+"#))]);
+    assert!(shadowed.diagnostics.iter().any(|d| d.code == "E_QUARRY_TYPE" && d.message.contains("int ?")),
+        "a user helper named count must not create builtin provenance: {:#?}", shadowed.diagnostics);
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn matching_role_guard_narrows_only_the_authorized_keyed_total() {
+    let source = r#"
+table entries:
+  owner: principal
+  public
+  online only
+table staff:
+  principal: principal
+  role: enum('finance')
+  unique principal, role
+  read <- .principal = viewer
+  delete <- .principal = viewer
+  online only
+view totals: count entries by .owner
+  read <- exists staff[principal = viewer, role = 'finance']
+  online only
+query raw(owner: principal):
+  return totals[owner]
+query guarded(owner: principal):
+  require exists staff[principal = viewer, role = 'finance'] else NOT_FINANCE
+  return totals[owner] + 1
+"#;
+    let bound = checked(source);
+    assert_eq!(bound.programs.iter().find(|program| program.program.name == "raw").unwrap().result, Ty::Int.optional());
+    assert_eq!(bound.programs.iter().find(|program| program.program.name == "guarded").unwrap().result, Ty::Int);
+    let mut engine = Engine::memory(bound.schema, bound.programs.into_iter().map(|program| program.program)).unwrap();
+    engine.seed([("entries".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([
+        ("id", Value::Id("one".into())), ("owner", Value::Id("bob".into())),
+    ]))]).unwrap();
+    let raw = |engine: &mut Engine, owner: &str| engine.query("raw", Context::new("alice", BTreeMap::from([
+        ("owner".into(), Value::Id(owner.into())),
+    ]))).unwrap().data;
+    assert_eq!(raw(&mut engine, "bob"), Value::Null, "a hidden stored total is not disclosed");
+    assert_eq!(raw(&mut engine, "nobody"), Value::Null, "a hidden miss is indistinguishable from a hidden hit");
+    engine.seed([("staff".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([
+        ("id", Value::Id("finance".into())), ("principal", Value::Id("alice".into())),
+        ("role", Value::String("finance".into())),
+    ]))]).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(raw(&mut engine, "bob"), Value::Int(1));
+    assert_eq!(raw(&mut engine, "nobody"), Value::Int(0), "an authorized keyed miss has the count identity");
+    assert_eq!(engine.query("guarded", Context::new("alice", BTreeMap::from([
+        ("owner".into(), Value::Id("nobody".into())),
+    ]))).unwrap().data, Value::Int(1));
+
+    let stale = compile(&[("schema.q".into(), format!(r#"{source}
+mutation stale(owner: principal, grant: staff):
+  require exists staff[principal = viewer, role = 'finance'] else NOT_FINANCE
+  delete staff[grant]
+  return totals[owner] + 1
+"#))]);
+    assert!(stale.diagnostics.iter().any(|diagnostic| diagnostic.code == "E_QUARRY_TYPE"
+        && diagnostic.message.contains("int ?")), "a write must invalidate the role proof: {:#?}", stale.diagnostics);
+}

+#[test]
+fn rounded_division_is_exact_signed_and_keeps_numeric_types() {
+    let source = r#"
+query rounded():
+  return [
+    divide(5, 2, 'toward-zero'), divide(5, 2, 'away-from-zero'),
+    divide(5, 2, 'floor'), divide(5, 2, 'ceiling'),
+    divide(5, 2, 'half-away-from-zero'), divide(5, 2, 'half-even'),
+    divide(7, 2, 'half-even'), divide(-5, 2, 'half-away-from-zero'),
+    divide(-5, 2, 'floor'), divide(-5, 2, 'ceiling'),
+    divide(5, -2, 'floor'), divide(5, -2, 'ceiling'),
+    divide(7, 3, 'half-even'), divide(8, 3, 'half-even')
+  ]
+query decimalValue(value: decimal 2):
+  return divide(value, 2, 'half-even')
+query moneyValue(value: money USD 2):
+  return divide(value, 2, 'half-even')
+query scaled(numerator: int, denominator: int):
+  return [
+    divide(numerator, denominator, 2, 'half-even'),
+    divide(numerator, denominator, 2, 'half-away-from-zero')
+  ]
+query wide(numerator: int, denominator: int):
+  return divide(numerator, denominator, 12, 'half-even')
+query scaleZero(numerator: int, denominator: int):
+  return divide(numerator, denominator, 0, 'half-even')
+query scaledOverflow():
+  return divide(9007199254740991, 1, 1, 'half-even')
+query zero():
+  return divide(1, 0, 'half-even')
+"#;
+    let bound = checked(source);
+    assert_eq!(bound.programs.iter().find(|p| p.program.name == "decimalValue").unwrap().result, Ty::Decimal(2));
+    assert_eq!(bound.programs.iter().find(|p| p.program.name == "moneyValue").unwrap().result, Ty::Money("USD".into(), 2));
+    let mut engine = Engine::memory(bound.schema, bound.programs.into_iter().map(|p| p.program)).unwrap();
+    let values = engine.query("rounded", Context::new("alice", BTreeMap::new())).unwrap().data;
+    assert_eq!(values, Value::Array([2, 3, 2, 3, 3, 2, 4, -3, -3, -2, -3, -2, 2, 3].into_iter().map(Value::Int).collect()));
+    for name in ["decimalValue", "moneyValue"] {
+        let value = engine.query(name, Context::new("alice", BTreeMap::from([("value".into(), Value::Int(5))]))).unwrap().data;
+        assert_eq!(value, Value::Int(2), "{name}");
+    }
+    let scaled = |engine: &mut Engine, numerator, denominator| engine.query("scaled", Context::new("alice", BTreeMap::from([
+        ("numerator".into(), Value::Int(numerator)), ("denominator".into(), Value::Int(denominator)),
+    ]))).unwrap().data;
+    assert_eq!(scaled(&mut engine, 101, 2), Value::Array(vec![Value::Int(5050), Value::Int(5050)]));
+    assert_eq!(scaled(&mut engine, -101, 2), Value::Array(vec![Value::Int(-5050), Value::Int(-5050)]));
+    assert_eq!(scaled(&mut engine, 1, 8), Value::Array(vec![Value::Int(12), Value::Int(13)]));
+    assert_eq!(scaled(&mut engine, -1, 8), Value::Array(vec![Value::Int(-12), Value::Int(-13)]));
+    assert_eq!(engine.query("wide", Context::new("alice", BTreeMap::from([
+        ("numerator".into(), Value::Int(snapback4_core::value::I53_MAX)),
+        ("denominator".into(), Value::Int(snapback4_core::value::I53_MAX)),
+    ]))).unwrap().data, Value::Int(1_000_000_000_000), "the wide scaled intermediate is not restricted to i53");
+    assert_eq!(engine.query("scaleZero", Context::new("alice", BTreeMap::from([
+        ("numerator".into(), Value::Int(5)), ("denominator".into(), Value::Int(2)),
+    ]))).unwrap().data, Value::Int(2));
+    assert_eq!(engine.query("scaledOverflow", Context::new("alice", BTreeMap::new())).unwrap_err().code, "E_OVERFLOW");
+    assert_eq!(engine.query("zero", Context::new("alice", BTreeMap::new())).unwrap_err().code, "E_DIV_ZERO");
+
+    use snapback4_core::ir::{Builtin, Expr, Program, ProgramKind, Rounding, Stmt};
+    let overflow = Program {
+        name: "overflow".into(), kind: ProgramKind::Query, args: BTreeMap::new(),
+        read_time_granularity_ms: None, native: false, returned_shapes: BTreeMap::new(),
+        body: vec![Stmt::Return(Expr::Builtin { builtin: Builtin::Divide { rounding: Rounding::TowardZero, scale: None },
+            args: vec![Expr::Literal(Value::Int(i64::MIN)), Expr::Literal(Value::Int(-1))] })],
+    };
+    let mut raw = Engine::memory(Default::default(), [overflow]).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(raw.query("overflow", Context::new("alice", BTreeMap::new())).unwrap_err().code, "E_OVERFLOW");
+
+    for bad in ["divide(1, 2, 'nearest')", "divide(1, 2, mode)", "divide(1, divisor, 'half-even')",
+        "divide(1, 2, 13, 'half-even')", "divide(1, 2, scale, 'half-even')"] {
+        let source = if bad.contains("mode") { format!("query bad(mode: enum('half-even')):\n  return {bad}\n") }
+            else if bad.contains("scale") { format!("query bad(scale: int):\n  return {bad}\n") }
+            else if bad.contains("divisor") { format!("query bad(divisor: decimal 2):\n  return {bad}\n") }
+            else { format!("query bad():\n  return {bad}\n") };
+        let bound = compile(&[("bad.q".into(), source)]);
+        assert!(bound.diagnostics.iter().any(|d| d.code == "E_QUARRY_TYPE"), "{bad}: {:#?}", bound.diagnostics);
+    }
+}

diff --git a/snapback4/crates/snapback4-core/src/engine/postgres/maintained_identity_upgrade.rs b/snapback4/crates/snapback4-core/src/engine/postgres/maintained_identity_upgrade.rs

--- /dev/null
+++ b/snapback4/crates/snapback4-core/src/engine/postgres/maintained_identity_upgrade.rs
@@ -0,0 +1,49 @@
+//! Atomic adoption of the maintained-row address function in the evaluation
+//! adapter. The marker and generation publish in the same writer transaction
+//! as the target rebuild, so no writer can observe mixed legacy/digest ids.
+use super::*;
+
+pub(super) fn install(
+    tx: &store::Tx<'_>,
+    schema: &Schema,
+    creating: bool,
+    generation: u64,
+) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
+    let current = tx.query(
+        "SELECT maintained_identity_version FROM _backend WHERE singleton",
+        &[],
+    )?[0].get::<_, Option<&str>>(0).map(str::to_owned);
+    if current.as_deref() == Some(crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_VERSION) {
+        return Ok(generation);
+    }
+
+    let aggregates: Vec<_> = schema.maintains.iter()
+        .filter(|maintain| maintain.private.is_none() && maintain.row_key.is_none())
+        .cloned()
+        .collect();
+    if !creating && !aggregates.is_empty() {
+        let mut runner = Runner::new(
+            tx,
+            schema,
+            Context::system().at(crate::now_ms()),
+            Meter::new(Ceilings::unbounded(), Cut::Abort),
+            tx.next_seq()?,
+        );
+        runner.event_free = true;
+        for maintain in &aggregates {
+            runner.rebuild_maintain(maintain)?;
+        }
+    }
+
+    let generation = if creating || aggregates.is_empty() {
+        generation
+    } else {
+        generation.checked_add(1)
+            .ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Generation("generation overflow".into()))?
+    };
+    tx.execute(
+        "UPDATE _backend SET maintained_identity_version=$1, generation=$2 WHERE singleton",
+        &[&crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_VERSION, &store::signed(generation)?],
+    )?;
+    Ok(generation)
+}

+    engine.load([("entries".into(), object([("id", Value::Id("entry".into())), ("bucket", Value::Int(7))]))]).unwrap();
+    let digest = crate::schema::maintained_id(&[Value::Int(7)]);
+    let legacy = crate::value::canonical_json(&[Value::Int(7)]);
+    let target = engine.schema.tables["totals"].clone();
+    let generation = engine.generation();
+    let tx = engine.store.transaction(Some(WriteMode::Serialized)).unwrap();
+    let old = tx.get("totals", &digest).unwrap().expect("current aggregate");
+    tx.delete("totals", &target, &old).unwrap();
+    let mut old = old;
+    if let Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields) = &mut old {
+        fields.insert("id".into(), Value::Id(legacy.clone()));
+    }
+    tx.put("totals", &target, &old, None).unwrap();
+    tx.execute("UPDATE _backend SET maintained_identity_version=NULL WHERE singleton", &[]).unwrap();
+    tx.commit().unwrap();
+    drop(engine);
+
+    let mut reopened = PostgresEngine::open(Client::connect(&url, postgres::NoTls).unwrap(), &name).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(reopened.generation(), generation + 1);
+    let tx = reopened.store.transaction(None).unwrap();
+    assert!(tx.get("totals", &legacy).unwrap().is_none());
+    let rebuilt = tx.get("totals", &digest).unwrap().expect("digest aggregate");
+    assert_eq!(rebuilt.field("value").unwrap(), &Value::Int(1));
+    tx.rollback().unwrap();
+}

 use std::collections::BTreeMap;
 
+const EXPIRY_TABLE_CURSOR: &str = "$expiry-table";
+
+/// Rotate a sweep's table order after the last table that consumed a bounded
+/// visit. Per-table row cursors alone can starve every later table when an
+/// earlier table contains a permanently restricted due row.
+pub(crate) fn resume_expiry_tables(
+    mut tables: Vec<String>,
+    cursors: &BTreeMap<String, Vec<Value>>,
+) -> Vec<String> {
+    let after = cursors
+        .get(EXPIRY_TABLE_CURSOR)
+        .and_then(|cursor| cursor.first())
+        .and_then(|value| value.as_str().ok());
+    if let Some(index) = after.and_then(|after| tables.iter().position(|table| table == after)) {
+        let next = (index + 1) % tables.len().max(1);
+        tables.rotate_left(next);
+    }
+    tables
+}
+
+pub(crate) fn mark_expiry_table(cursors: &mut BTreeMap<String, Vec<Value>>, table: &str) {
+    cursors.insert(EXPIRY_TABLE_CURSOR.into(), vec![Value::String(table.into())]);
+}

+    /// Whether a read-through child remains outside a delete's cascade
+    /// closure. Children in `deleting` are removed first by deletion_order and
+    /// therefore do not physically retain their parent.

     ) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {

             .children(parent)
             .map(|(n, _, _)| n.clone())
             .collect();
+        // At most `deleting.len()` matching rows can be skipped across a

+        self.authorized_scan(&[(MeterKind::Examined, probes), (MeterKind::Steps, probes), (MeterKind::HeapBytes, heap)], |runner, scope| {

+                occupied |= rows.into_iter().any(|(row, _)| row.field("id").ok().and_then(|id| id.as_str().ok())
+                    .is_none_or(|child| !deleting.contains(&(name.clone(), child.to_owned()))));
             }
             Ok(occupied)
         })

+/// The copied corpus is a frozen image of the pre-digest store. Translate
+/// maintained target identities at the adapter boundary so its logical values
+/// remain an oracle for the current address function. Other row ids retain
+/// their exact frozen spelling.
+fn legacy_maintained_ids(schema: &Schema, rows: &[ReceiptRow]) -> Result<BTreeMap<String, String>, String> {
+    let mut ids = BTreeMap::new();
+    for receipt in rows {
+        let Some(maintain) = schema.maintains.iter().find(|maintain| maintain.target == receipt.table && maintain.row_key.is_none()) else { continue };
+        let old = match receipt.row.field("id") {
+            Ok(Value::Id(id)) => id,
+            Ok(_) => return Err(format!("{}.id is not an id", receipt.table)),
+            Err(error) => return Err(format!("{}.id: {error}", receipt.table)),
+        };
+        let key = maintain.by.iter().map(|field| receipt.row.field(field).cloned().map_err(|error| format!("{}.{}: {error}", receipt.table, field))).collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()?;
+        let new = snapback4_core::schema::maintained_id(&key);
+        if let Some(prior) = ids.insert(old.clone(), new.clone())
+            && prior != new
+        {
+            return Err(format!("legacy id {old} names more than one maintained group"));
+        }
+    }
+    Ok(ids)
+}
+
+fn translate_legacy_maintained_row(schema: &Schema, table: &str, row: &mut Value, ids: &BTreeMap<String, String>) {
+    if !schema.maintains.iter().any(|maintain| maintain.target == table && maintain.row_key.is_none()) { return; }
+    let (Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields)) = row else { return };
+    let Some(Value::Id(id)) = fields.get_mut("id") else { return };
+    if let Some(replacement) = ids.get(id) {
+        *id = replacement.clone();
+    }
+}
+
+fn translate_legacy_maintained_expected(expected: &mut Expected, ids: &BTreeMap<String, String>) -> Result<(), String> {
+    if ids.is_empty() || expected.error_code.is_some() { return Ok(()); }
+    let Some(canonical) = &expected.canonical_result else { return Ok(()) };
+    let mut value: Value = serde_json::from_str(canonical).map_err(|error| error.to_string())?;
+    translate_legacy_maintained_result(&mut value, ids);
+    expected.canonical_result = Some(snapback4_core::value::canonical_json(&value));
+    Ok(())
+}
+
+fn translate_legacy_maintained_result(value: &mut Value, ids: &BTreeMap<String, String>) {
+    match value {
+        Value::Id(id) => {
+            if let Some(replacement) = ids.get(id) {
+                *id = replacement.clone();
+            }
+        }
+        Value::Array(values) => values.iter_mut().for_each(|value| translate_legacy_maintained_result(value, ids)),
+        Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields) => fields.values_mut().for_each(|value| translate_legacy_maintained_result(value, ids)),
+        _ => {}
+    }
+}
+
 /// The schema validator exposes a path/message instead of SB2's code.
 /// Translate only this observed, typed admission category. A schema that
 /// unexpectedly starts validating still runs and fails its refusal oracle.

                 ("exists", Value::Bool(false)), ("row", Value::Null),

                     ("__proto__", Value::Null), ("toString", Value::Null), ("value", Value::Int(1)),

The published touched set includes every derived destination, and the reply omits every row the actions changed. Cascade and set null are refused into tables that feed a maintained sum, have any field-owned column, or belong to a timeline in any role. `set null` is refused where any rule hops through the column. A device needs the referencing group acquired, not only readable. The removal order follows cascade and `read through` edges, whose union must be acyclic. `check` names the read prerequisite where a deleter may not be a reader (`N_DELETE_NEEDS_READ`). Dispositions in §11); 2026-10-12 (revision 1: folds one blind round, GPT NOT READY and Muse READY WITH CHANGES. `on delete keep` is added for deliberate history. A delete evaluates its whole cascade closure before it refuses, so a diamond or a sibling reference never refuses spuriously, and the reported reference is chosen in schema order, never by hidden iteration order. `set null` may clear only a column that carries no authority anywhere in the schema. Every published trace of a delete with actions — touched tables, change footprints, event counts, the physical authorization allowance — is fixed by the schema. The reservation reuses the exported source-write price, so a device consumes the same price the server computes. A null-exempt cap never proves a population bound. Cascade and set null into append-only, field-owned or unpriced children are refused. The postcondition is scoped to the rows present when the delete runs. Dispositions in §11); 2026-10-12 (draft)
 **Related:** [LLP 3000](./3000-snapback4.explainer.md) (§7, 2026-09-13 "reference IDs have no implicit foreign-key check": this RFC amends its delete half), [LLP 3000.036](./3000.036-what-the-app-farm-asks-of-the-rule-language.rfc.md) (§15.8, the open question this answers; §16.2, the zero-count guard), [LLP 3000.014](./3000.014-a-child-reads-through-its-parent.rfc.md) (§3, a child lives within its parent; §5, predicted parent deletes; §6, `E_PARENT_HAS_CHILDREN`), [LLP 3000.015](./3000.015-shared-baseline-for-snapback5.spec.md) (§2, one authorization law: work whose shape depends on unreadable rows is charged from a fixed reservation), [LLP 3000.022](./3000.022-delivery-the-sdk-reports.rfc.md) (§14.3, one exported source-write price), [LLP 3000.023](./3000.023-answers-stay-on-screen.rfc.md) (§12, change evidence), [LLP 3000.007](./3000.007-relaxed-quarry-and-explicit-residency.rfc.md) (§20.5, held-group proofs for device writes), [LLP 3000.035](./3000.035-quarry-semantics-in-lean.plan.md) (§5.2, the Lean model)

+#[test]
+fn read_through_closure_probe_is_admitted_before_a_low_ceiling_delete() {
+    let source = r#"
+table roots:
+  public
+  delete <- allow
+table children:
+  root: roots on delete cascade
+  cap 2 by root
+  public
+table grandchildren:
+  child: children on delete cascade
+  cap 2 by child
+  immutable child
+  read through .child
+mutation drop(id: roots):
+  delete roots[id]
+"#;
+    let world = || {
+        let mut e = engine(source);
+        e.seed_at([
+            ("roots".into(), object([("id", id("p"))])),
+            ("children".into(), object([("id", id("c")), ("root", id("p"))])),
+            ("grandchildren".into(), object([("id", id("g")), ("child", id("c"))])),
+        ], 0).unwrap();
+        e
+    };
+    let context = || Context::new("dev:alice", BTreeMap::from([("id".into(), id("p"))])).at(100);
+    let mut complete = world();
+    let sent = complete.mutate("drop", None, context()).unwrap();
+    assert!(matches!(sent.state, WriteState::Sent { .. }), "{:?}", sent.state);
+
+    let mut cut = world();
+    let mut ceilings = cut.ceilings();
+    ceilings.examined = sent.metered.examined - 1;
+    cut.set_ceilings(ceilings);
+    let refused = cut.mutate("drop", None, context()).unwrap();
+    assert!(matches!(refused.state, WriteState::Failed { ref why, .. } if why.code == "E_BOUND"), "{:?}", refused.state);
+    assert_eq!(cut.store().rows("roots").unwrap().len(), 1);
+    assert_eq!(cut.store().rows("children").unwrap().len(), 1);
+    assert_eq!(cut.store().rows("grandchildren").unwrap().len(), 1);
+}

+#[test]
+fn same_id_replacement_reloads_maintained_columns_after_cascade_retirement() {
+    let source = r#"
+table roots:
+  expiresAt: time ?
+  by byExpiry: expiresAt
+  expire at .expiresAt
+  childCount: count children by root
+  public
+  insert <- allow
+table children:
+  root: roots on delete cascade
+  cap 4 by root
+  public
+mutation replace():
+  insert roots {id: 'same', expiresAt: null}
+"#;
+    let mut e = engine(source);
+    e.seed_at([
+        ("roots".into(), object([("id", id("same")), ("expiresAt", Value::Int(10))])),
+        ("children".into(), object([("id", id("child")), ("root", id("same"))])),
+    ], 0).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("roots").unwrap()[0].field("childCount").unwrap(), &Value::Int(1));
+
+    let replaced = e.mutate("replace", None, Context::new("dev:alice", BTreeMap::new()).at(100)).unwrap();
+    assert!(matches!(replaced.state, WriteState::Sent { .. }), "{:?}", replaced.state);
+    let roots = e.store().rows("roots").unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(roots.len(), 1);
+    assert_eq!(roots[0].field("childCount").unwrap(), &Value::Int(0));
+    assert!(e.store().rows("children").unwrap().is_empty());
+}

+-- @ref LLP 3000.036.003#6 — born-expired and updated-expired final images retire in the writer transaction.
+/-- Rows whose final images a mutation changed. Commit-end expiry retirement
+is scoped to this set; pre-existing expired backlog remains for the ordinary
+sweep. -/
+abbrev ChangedRows := List (String × List Nat)
+
+structure MutationWorld where
+  store : Store
+  changed : ChangedRows := []
+
+def RWrite.explicitId? : RWrite → Option (String × List Nat)
+  | .insert t fields _ => match fields.lookup "id" with
+    | some (.s (.id rid)) => some (t, rid)
+    | _ => none
+  | .upsert t key patch =>
+    match key.lookup "id" with
+    | some (.s (.id rid)) => some (t, rid)
+    | _ => match patch.lookup "id" with
+      | some (.s (.id rid)) => some (t, rid)
+      | _ => none
+  | _ => none
+
+def changedFinalRows (sch : Schema) (before after : Store) : ChangedRows :=
+  sch.tables.flatMap fun td => (after td.name).filterMap fun row =>
+    match (before td.name).find? fun old => old.id == row.id with
+    | none => some (td.name, row.id)
+    | some old => if old == row then none else some (td.name, row.id)
+
+def mutationHooks : Hooks MutationWorld where
+  view cx w := visibleRowsAt cx.schema w.store cx.viewer cx.now
+  apply cx w rw := match applyWrite cx w.store rw with
+    | .error e => .error e
+    | .ok (value, store) =>
+      let changed := w.changed ++ changedFinalRows cx.schema w.store store
+      let changed := match rw.explicitId? with | some address => changed ++ [address] | none => changed

+def retireExpiredChanged (sch : Schema) (now : Int) : Store → ChangedRows → Except Stop Store
+  | s, [] => pure s

+    | none => retireExpiredChanged sch now s rest
+    | some td =>
+      match findRow (s t) [("id", .id rid)] with
+      | none => retireExpiredChanged sch now s rest
+      | some row =>
+        if expired td now row then do
+          let s ← refDeleteFrom sch (unexpiredStore sch s now) s t row
+          retireExpiredChanged sch now s rest
+        else retireExpiredChanged sch now s rest
+

 ## Summary
@@ -148,7 +148,15 @@ rows, writes the marker, and publishes a new semantic generation. A failure
 rolls back old rows, rebuilt rows, marker and generation together. Adoption
 advice counts the SQLite rebuild even when schema/program bytes are unchanged;
 the evaluation adapter performs the corresponding rebuild under its opening
-writer/head fence. Schemas with ordinary maintains require device capability
+writer/head fence. Before clearing targets, adoption derives each target's
+legacy-id-to-digest map to a fixed point over typed reference dependencies,
+then rewrites every surviving typed reference through those maps. Thus an
+aggregate grouped by a reference to another aggregate uses that referenced
+aggregate's new digest when deriving its own digest, and a table that refers
+to either rebuilt target does not dangle. A legacy id with no matching stored
+target stays opaque, preserving the existing dangling-reference contract.
+Reference rewrites, index updates, target rebuilds, marker and generation share
+the same transaction. Schemas with ordinary maintains require device capability
 `maintained-id-sha256-v1`; an older device is refused at the handshake before
 it can compute a legacy id and silently read a digest-addressed aggregate as
 zero.

+#[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
+fn has_legacy_maintained_reference(
+    kind: &crate::schema::ColumnType,
+    ids: &BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, String>>,
+) -> bool {
+    match kind {
+        crate::schema::ColumnType::Ref { table } => ids.get(table).is_some_and(|ids| !ids.is_empty()),
+        crate::schema::ColumnType::Optional(inner)
+        | crate::schema::ColumnType::List { of: inner, .. }
+        | crate::schema::ColumnType::ListRange { of: inner, .. } => has_legacy_maintained_reference(inner, ids),
+        _ => false,
+    }
+}
+
+#[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
+fn rewrite_legacy_maintained_reference(
+    kind: &crate::schema::ColumnType,
+    value: &mut Value,
+    ids: &BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, String>>,
+) -> bool {
+    match (kind, value) {
+        (crate::schema::ColumnType::Ref { table }, Value::Id(id)) => {
+            let Some(next) = ids.get(table).and_then(|ids| ids.get(id)) else { return false };
+            *id = next.clone();
+            true
+        }
+        (crate::schema::ColumnType::Optional(inner), value) => rewrite_legacy_maintained_reference(inner, value, ids),
+        (crate::schema::ColumnType::List { of, .. } | crate::schema::ColumnType::ListRange { of, .. }, Value::Array(values)) =>
+            values.iter_mut().fold(false, |changed, value| rewrite_legacy_maintained_reference(of, value, ids) || changed),
+        _ => false,
+    }
+}
+

+    /// Derive every legacy-to-digest aggregate id map to a fixed point, then
+    /// rewrite typed references before rebuilding the target rows. The fixed
+    /// point matters when one aggregate groups by a reference to another.
+    /// Every pass is inside the adoption writer transaction, so no reader can
+    /// observe a dangling intermediate reference.
+    #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
+    pub(crate) fn rewrite_legacy_maintained_references(&mut self, maintains: &[Maintain]) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
+        let mut legacy = Vec::new();
+        for maintain in maintains.iter().filter(|maintain| maintain.private.is_none() && maintain.row_key.is_none()) {
+            let target = self.schema.tables[&maintain.target].clone();
+            let fields: Vec<_> = maintain.group_fields().into_iter().map(|field| {
+                let kind = target.columns.get(&field).expect("validated maintain group").clone();
+                (field, kind)
+            }).collect();
+            let mut rows = Vec::new();
+            let mut bounds = Bounds::default();
+            loop {
+                let page = self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.scan(allowance, &maintain.target, "byId", &[], &bounds, Dir::Asc, 256))?;
+                if page.is_empty() { break; }
+                for (row, encoded) in page {
+                    bounds.after = crate::key::decode(&encoded);
+                    let old = row.field("id")?.as_str()?.to_owned();
+                    let key = fields.iter().map(|(field, kind)| Ok((kind.clone(), row.field(field)?.clone())))
+                        .collect::<Result<Vec<_>, RuntimeError>>()?;
+                    rows.push((old, key));
+                }
+            }
+            legacy.push((maintain.target.clone(), rows));
+        }
+
+        let mut ids: BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, String>> = BTreeMap::new();
+        let mut settled = false;
+        for _ in 0..=legacy.len() {
+            let mut next_ids: BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, String>> = BTreeMap::new();
+            for (target, rows) in &legacy {
+                let target_ids = next_ids.entry(target.clone()).or_default();
+                for (old, key) in rows {
+                    let key: Vec<_> = key.iter().map(|(kind, value)| {
+                        let mut value = value.clone();
+                        rewrite_legacy_maintained_reference(kind, &mut value, &ids);
+                        value
+                    }).collect();
+                    let next = maintained_id(&key);
+                    if old != &next { target_ids.insert(old.clone(), next); }
+                }
+            }
+            if next_ids == ids {
+                ids = next_ids;
+                settled = true;
+                break;
+            }
+            ids = next_ids;
+        }
+        if !settled {
+            return Err(RuntimeError::Schema("legacy aggregate identity references form a cycle".into()));
+        }
+
+        let references: Vec<_> = self.schema.tables.iter().filter_map(|(name, table)| {
+            let columns: Vec<_> = table.columns.iter().filter_map(|(column, kind)|
+                has_legacy_maintained_reference(kind, &ids).then(|| (column.clone(), kind.clone())))
+                .collect();
+            (!columns.is_empty()).then(|| (name.clone(), table.clone(), columns))
+        }).collect();
+        let mut rewritten = 0_u64;
+        for (name, table, columns) in references {
+            let mut bounds = Bounds::default();
+            loop {
+                let page = self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.scan(allowance, &name, "byId", &[], &bounds, Dir::Asc, 256))?;
+                if page.is_empty() { break; }
+                for (old, encoded) in page {
+                    bounds.after = crate::key::decode(&encoded);
+                    let mut next = old.clone();
+                    let mut changed = false;
+                    if let Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields) = &mut next {
+                        for (column, kind) in &columns {
+                            let Some(value) = fields.get_mut(column) else { continue };
+                            changed |= rewrite_legacy_maintained_reference(kind, value, &ids);
+                        }
+                    }
+                    if changed {
+                        self.tx.put(&name, &table, &next, Some(&old))?;
+                        rewritten = rewritten.saturating_add(1);
+                    }
+                }
+            }
+        }
+        Ok(rewritten)
+    }

+
+fn strip_maintained_identity_capability(mut wire: String) -> String {
+    let capability = "maintained-id-sha256-v1";
+    wire = wire.replace(&format!("\"{capability}\","), "")
+        .replace(&format!(",\"{capability}\""), "")
+        .replace(&format!("[{{\"Capabilities\":[\"{capability}\"]}}]"), "[]")
+        .replace(&format!("{{\"Capabilities\":[\"{capability}\"]}},"), "")
+        .replace(&format!(",{{\"Capabilities\":[\"{capability}\"]}}"), "");
+    assert!(!wire.contains(capability));
+    wire
 }

I’m checking the final call ordering and transaction boundaries, especially whether late blockers can occur after closure writes and whether transitive references survive rebuilds.

+This commit-end rule also covers a source of a row-keyed maintained view. The
+source's final image first reaches normal maintenance, then its expired image
+is retired through the common action path in the same transaction. No derived
+maintenance shortcut may physically remove that source before closure
+preflight: doing so would bypass a live `restrict` child and could orphan a
+`cascade` or `set null` child. The source contribution and its retirement
+cancel within the transaction, so an already-expired birth never enters a
+committed count basis. The execution retains at most one retirement key per
+changed source row; its allocation is charged when first retained and the
+program's existing rows-written ceiling bounds the commit-end walk.
+
 A live `restrict` child, or a physically retained read-through child outside
 the cascade closure but below a row in it, keeps the expired root physically
 stored and the sweep continues to later due keys. A read-through child inside

+    let row_view_expiry = r#"
+table conversations:
+  public
+  sync public
+table members:
+  conversation: conversations
+  principal: principal
+  cap 4 by conversation
+  public
+  sync public
+table messages:
+  conversation: conversations
+  ordinal: int
+  sender: principal
+  until: time ?
+  expire at .until
+  public
+  update <- allow
+  sync public
+view unread: count messages by members m
+  where .conversation = m.conversation and .sender != m.principal
+table cascadeKids:
+  message: messages on delete cascade
+  cap 1 by message
+  public
+  sync public
+table nullableKids:
+  message: messages ? on delete set null
+  cap 1 by message
+  public
+  sync public

+  update messages[message] { until: now }

+#[test]
+fn row_keyed_view_source_expiry_retires_through_reference_actions() {
+    let source = r#"
+table conversations:
+  public
+table members:
+  conversation: conversations
+  principal: principal
+  cap 4 by conversation
+  public
+table messages:
+  conversation: conversations
+  ordinal: int
+  sender: principal
+  until: time ?
+  expire at .until
+  public
+  update <- allow
+view unread: count messages by members m
+  where .conversation = m.conversation and .sender != m.principal
+table cascadeKids:
+  message: messages on delete cascade
+  cap 1 by message
+  public
+table nullableKids:
+  message: messages ? on delete set null
+  cap 1 by message
+  public
+table blockers:
+  message: messages
+  public
+mutation expire(message: messages):
+  update messages[message] { until: now }
+"#;
+    let mut e = engine(source);
+    e.seed_at([
+        ("conversations".into(), object([("id", id("c"))])),
+        ("members".into(), object([("id", id("member")), ("conversation", id("c")), ("principal", id("alice"))])),
+        ("messages".into(), object([("id", id("message")), ("conversation", id("c")), ("ordinal", Value::Int(1)), ("sender", id("bob")), ("until", Value::Null)])),
+        ("cascadeKids".into(), object([("id", id("cascade")), ("message", id("message"))])),
+        ("nullableKids".into(), object([("id", id("nullable")), ("message", id("message"))])),
+        ("blockers".into(), object([("id", id("blocker")), ("message", id("message"))])),
+    ], 0).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("unread").unwrap()[0].field("value").unwrap(), &Value::Int(1));
+
+    let context = || Context::new("dev:alice", BTreeMap::from([("message".into(), id("message"))])).at(100);
+    let refused = e.mutate("expire", None, context()).unwrap();
+    assert!(matches!(refused.state, WriteState::Failed { ref why, .. } if why.code == "E_REFERENCED"), "{:?}", refused.state);
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("messages").unwrap()[0].field("until").unwrap(), &Value::Null);
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("unread").unwrap()[0].field("value").unwrap(), &Value::Int(1));
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("cascadeKids").unwrap().len(), 1, "a refused commit rolls its cascade back");
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("nullableKids").unwrap()[0].field("message").unwrap(), &id("message"));
+
+    e.seed_delete("blockers", "blocker").unwrap();
+    let sent = e.mutate("expire", None, context()).unwrap();
+    assert!(matches!(sent.state, WriteState::Sent { .. }), "{:?}", sent.state);
+    assert!(e.store().rows("messages").unwrap().is_empty());
+    assert!(e.store().rows("cascadeKids").unwrap().is_empty());
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("nullableKids").unwrap()[0].field("message").unwrap(), &Value::Null);
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("unread").unwrap()[0].field("value").unwrap(), &Value::Int(0));
+}

    61	        // A directly supplied field is a payload error before any lookup;
    62	        // only an upsert's copied address waits for insert authority.
    63	        if upsert_index.is_none() && supplied_sequence.is_err() { return supplied_sequence.map(|_| false); }
    64	        let supplied = row.clone();
    65	        let row = self.with_defaults(table_name, row)?;
    66	        if self.schema.tables[table_name].ephemeral.is_some() { self.meter.heap(row.heap_bytes())?; }
    67	        let row = row.ephemeral(&self.schema.tables[table_name], self.context.now.unwrap_or(0))?;
    68	        // @ref LLP 3000.014#4-the-capture — reserve, then stamp the parent capture before any rule sees the image.
    69	        self.reserve_capture(&self.schema.tables[table_name])?;
    70	        let row = self.capture_insert(table_name, row)?;
    71	        let table = &self.schema.tables[table_name];
    72	        let independent = !table.sequences.is_empty() && !super::rules::deciding_fields(table_name, table, &table.rules.insert)
    73	            .iter().any(|field| table.sequences.contains_key(field));
    74	        // An independent denial must never consult a hidden read witness.
    75	        let authorized = independent && self.check_rule(table_name, Effect::Insert, None, &row)?;
    76	        if independent && !authorized {
    77	            return Err(if upsert_index.is_some() { self.no_write_target() } else { self.rule_refusal(table_name, Effect::Insert, "insert rule") });
    78	        }
    79	        if !table.sequences.is_empty() {
    80	            // Admission reserves the worst case before either read verdict;
    81	            // restoring a refusal alone cannot hide a boundary abort.
    82	            // An independent insert rule was already prepaid and evaluated.
    83	            // Only still-pending checks belong in this preflight allowance.
    84	            let insert_checks = if authorized { 0 } else { 1 + u64::from(upsert_index.is_some() && supplied_sequence.is_ok()) };
    85	            self.reserve_sequence_authorization(table, &row, insert_checks)?;
    86	        }
    87	        // @ref LLP 3000.015#2 — an unreadable allocation cannot expose counter,
    88	        // uniqueness or cap state, even to a principal allowed to insert.
    89	        if !self.sequence_insert_readable(table_name, &row)? {
    90	            self.refusing_clause(table_name, "sequence read authority");
    91	            return Err(if upsert_index.is_some() { self.no_write_target() } else { self.rule_refusal(table_name, Effect::Insert, "sequence read authority") });
    92	        }
    93	        if let Err(error) = supplied_sequence {
    94	            // @ref LLP 3000.007#17 — absent upserts decide insert authority before field diagnostics.
    95	            // A target key may supply an ordinal even when the patch does not.
    96	            if !authorized && !self.check_rule(table_name, Effect::Insert, None, &row)? {
    97	                return Err(if upsert_index.is_some() { self.no_write_target() } else { self.rule_refusal(table_name, Effect::Insert, "insert rule") });
    98	            }
    99	            return Err(if upsert_index.is_some() { self.no_write_target() } else { error });
   100	        }
   101	        if upsert_index.is_some() {
   102	            self.authorize_fields(table_name, &row, &supplied).map_err(|_| self.no_write_target())?;
   103	        } else { self.authorize_fields(table_name, &row, &supplied)?; }
   104	        // The image copy an event slot costs is the writer's own supplied bytes (LLP 3000.015 §1).
   105	        let image_bytes = row.heap_bytes();
   106	        let (row, sequence_full) = self.sequence_fields(table_name, row)?;
   107	        let row = self.receipt_insert_fields(table_name, row)?;
   108	        if let Some(index) = upsert_index {
   109	            if self.device { self.prove_upsert_insert(table_name, index, &row)?; }
   110	            // Preserve upsert's target preflight before the ordinary insert checks;
   111	            // only this first authority refusal is an undisclosed target miss.
   112	            if !authorized && !self.check_rule(table_name, Effect::Insert, None, &row)? { return Err(self.no_write_target()); }
   113	            if sequence_full { return Err(super::sequences::exhausted()); }
   114	            // Engine event slots are stamped after predecessor/sequence checks,
   115	            // just as on an ordinary insert; preflight validates authored fields.
   116	            if let Err(error) = super::validate::validate_before_slots(self.schema, table_name, &row) {
   117	                return Err(if matches!(error, RuntimeError::Input(_)) && !self.context.is_system() { self.no_write_target() } else { error });
   118	            }
   119	        }
   120	        if !authorized && !self.check_rule(table_name, Effect::Insert, None, &row)? {
   121	            return Err(self.rule_refusal(table_name, Effect::Insert, "insert rule"));
   122	        }
   123	        // Retry keys independent of engine allocation still identify a no-op
   124	        // at the ceiling. Never use the clamped authority candidate as a key.
   125	        if sequence_full && if_absent {
   126	            let table = &self.schema.tables[table_name];
   127	            for (name, index) in table.indexes.iter().filter(|(_, index)| {
   128	                index.unique && index.columns().iter().all(|column| !table.sequences.contains_key(column))
   129	            }) {
   130	                let key = index_values(index, &row);
   131	                if key.contains(&Value::Null) { continue; }
   132	                if self.collision_lookup(table_name, name, index, &key, None, Effect::Insert)?.is_some() {
   133	                    self.observe_sequence_columns(table_name, &row, &index.columns(), true)?;
   134	                    return Ok(false);
   135	                }
   136	            }
   137	        }
   138	        if sequence_full { return Err(super::sequences::exhausted()); }
   139	        let row = self.record_insert(table_name, row)?;
   140	        let row = self.with_asset_facts(table_name, row, None, None)?;
   141	        if if_absent {
   142	            for (name, index) in table.indexes.iter().filter(|(_, index)| index.unique) {
   143	                let key = index_values(index, &row);
   144	                if key.iter().any(|value| *value == Value::Null) {
   145	                    continue;
   146	                }
   147	                if self.collision_lookup(table_name, name, index, &key, None, Effect::Insert)?.is_some() {
   148	                    self.observe_sequence_columns(table_name, &row, &index.columns(), true)?;
   149	                    return Ok(false);
   150	                }
   151	            }
   152	        }
   153	        let id = row.field("id")?.as_str()?.to_owned();
   154	        // @ref LLP 3000.007#20.5 — if-absent's insert arm needs the same image, unique-population and cap proof as upsert.
   155	        // Upsert mints its insert id; if-absent may instead supply one.
   156	        // Only a freshly minted id can skip the primary-key absence proof.
   157	        let minted = self.context.minted_ids.contains(&id);
   158	        let proof = if !self.device { None } else if minted {
   159	            table.indexes.iter().find(|(name, index)| {
   160	                    name.as_str() != "byId" && index.unique && !index_values(index, &row).contains(&Value::Null)
   161	                })
   162	                .map(|(name, _)| name.as_str()).or_else(|| {
   163	                    table.constraints.iter().any(|c| matches!(c, Constraint::Cap { .. })).then_some("byId")
   164	                })
   165	        } else { Some("byId") };
   166	        if if_absent && let Some(index) = proof.or(self.device.then_some("byId")) {
   167	            self.prove_upsert_insert(table_name, index, &row)?;
   168	        }
   169	        // An upsert has already resolved this exact address (or minted the id)
   170	        // and reserved both target proofs. Retiring an expired predecessor
   171	        // uses that same allowance, not a third read-rule reservation.
   172	        let collision_probes = if upsert_index.is_some() { 0 } else { super::rules::rule_probes(&table.rules.read) };
   173	        let has_children = self.schema.children(table_name).next().is_some()
   174	            || self.schema.is_referenced(table_name);
   175	        let predecessor = self.authorized_scan(&[(MeterKind::RuleProbes, collision_probes)], |runner, allowance| {
   176	            let existing = runner.tx.get(allowance, table_name, &id)?;
   177	            if let Some(row) = &existing {
   178	                if !runner.expired(table, row) { runner.visible_collision(table_name, row, Effect::Insert, "unique id")?; }
   179	                // @ref LLP 3000.014#3-a-child-lives-within-its-parent — an expired birth with physical
   180	                // children collides like a live birth: check the old image's authority under the same
   181	                // reservation, without treating expiry as denial. A non-reader never probes the children.
   182	                else if has_children && !runner.check_rule(table_name, Effect::Read, None, row)? {
   183	                    return Err(runner.rule_refusal(table_name, Effect::Insert, "unique id"));
   184	                }
   185	            }
   186	            Ok(existing)
   187	        })?;
   188	        if predecessor.as_ref().is_none_or(|old| self.expired(table, old)) && has_children {
   189	            let mark = self.meter.mark();
   190	            if self.physical_children(table_name, &Value::Id(id.clone()))? {
   191	                // The bounded probes have completed. Their occupancy is not
   192	                // disclosed by the collision's logical meter or heap peak.
   193	                self.meter.restore(mark);
   194	                return Err(if predecessor.is_some() {
   195	                    RuntimeError::Constraint(format!("{table_name} already has a row with id {id}"))
   196	                } else { self.rule_refusal(table_name, Effect::Insert, "parent identity has stored children") });
   197	            }
   198	        }
   199	        if let Some(existing) = &predecessor {
   200	            if !self.expired(table, &existing) {
   201	                return Err(RuntimeError::Constraint(format!("{table_name} already has a row with id {id}")));
   202	            }
   203	            // The expired predecessor is internal authorization work, not a
   204	            // disclosed examination (LLP 3000.015 §§1–2).
   205	            self.retire_expired_row(table_name, existing)?;
   206	        }
   207	        // Retiring an expired predecessor can cascade a source row whose
   208	        // contribution determines this image's maintained columns. Initialize
   209	        // them from the post-retirement private totals. Maintained columns are
   210	        // forbidden from constraints and authority, so the earlier collision
   211	        // and authorization preflights need only the authored image.
   212	        let row = self.birth_columns(table_name, row)?;
   213	        super::validate::validate_before_slots(self.schema, table_name, &row)?;
   214	        // @ref LLP 3000.007#20.5 — an authored plain insert predicts unproved; a later refusal is then the server's
   215	        // to report. The engine's own timeline writes are not the author's prediction.
   216	        if let Some(index) = proof.filter(|_| {
   217	            !if_absent && upsert_index.is_none() && !self.unproved_write && self.timeline_authority.is_none()
   218	        }) {
   219	            // An earlier unknown fact already makes this prediction unproved.
   220	            // Otherwise the proof's own unknown fact is not the prediction's.
   221	            self.unproved_write = self.missing_fact.is_some();
   222	            if !self.unproved_write {
   223	                let beyond = self.beyond_horizon;
   224	                let proved = self.device_work(|runner| runner.prove_upsert_insert(table_name, index, &row));
   225	                (self.beyond_horizon, self.missing_fact) = (beyond, None);
   226	                match proved { Err(RuntimeError::Prediction(_)) => self.unproved_write = true, other => other? }
   227	            }
   228	        }
   229	        // The server's same-id expired replacement preserves occupancy in
   230	        // unchanged cap groups. A device cannot rely on an expired predecessor.
   231	        self.check_constraints(table_name, predecessor.as_ref(), &row, Effect::Insert)?;
   232	        self.commit_sequences(table_name, &row)?;
   233	        self.commit_receipt_counter(table_name, &row)?;
   234	        let row = self.prepare_event_slots(table_name, None, row, image_bytes)?;
   235	        validate_row(self.schema, table_name, &row)?;
   236	        let entries = self.maintain_scratch(self.contribution_heap(table), |runner| {
   237	            runner.tx.put(table_name, table, &row, None)
   238	        })?;
   239	        self.charge_source_indexes(table, None, Some(&row), entries)?;
   240	        self.row_changed(table_name, None, Some(&row), Origin::Source)?;
   241	        Ok(true)
   242	    }
   243	
   244	    pub(super) fn update(&mut self, table_name: &str, key: &Value, patch: Supplied) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   245	        if self.device && self.schema.tables[table_name].not_before.is_some() {
   246	            return Err(RuntimeError::Prediction(
   247	                "a mutation touching a `not before` table runs on the server".into(),
   248	            ));
   249	        }
   250	        self.target_attempt(table_name, |runner| {
   251	            runner.update_attempt(table_name, key, patch)
   252	        })
   253	    }
   254	
   255	    fn update_attempt(&mut self, table_name: &str, key: &Value, patch: Supplied) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   256	        self.refuse_engine_owned(table_name, Effect::Update)?;
   257	        self.refuse_receipt_fields(table_name, &patch, false)?;
   258	        self.refuse_recorded(table_name, &patch)?;
   259	        super::sequences::refuse_fields(&self.schema.tables[table_name], table_name, &patch)?;
   260	        if patch.as_object()?.contains_key("id") {
   261	            return Err(RuntimeError::Input(format!("{table_name} update patch cannot change id")));
   262	        }
   263	        let id = key.as_str()?;
   264	        self.reserve_target_resolution(table_name, self.schema.table(table_name).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Schema(format!("missing table {table_name}")))?, &patch, false)?;
   265	        let Some(old) = self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| {
   266	            runner.fetch_write_target(allowance, table_name, id)
   267	        })? else {
   268	            return Err(self.write_miss(table_name, "byId", &[key.clone()]));
   269	        };
   270	        if self.device && self.schema.tables[table_name].sync.is_none() { return Err(self.write_miss(table_name, "byId", &[key.clone()])); }
   271	        let readable = !self.inactive_write_target(table_name, &old)?
   272	            && self.check_rule(table_name, Effect::Read, None, &old)?;
   273	        let patch = self.ignore_hidden_immutable_patch(table_name, patch, readable)?;
   274	        let (new, copy) = self.merge_patch(table_name, &old, &patch, readable)?;
   275	        self.replace(table_name, old, new, readable, &patch, copy)
   276	    }
   277	
   278	    pub(super) fn upsert(&mut self, table_name: &str, key: &Value, row: Supplied) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   279	        if self.device && self.schema.tables[table_name].not_before.is_some() {
   280	            return Err(RuntimeError::Prediction(
   281	                "a mutation touching a `not before` table runs on the server".into(),
   282	            ));
   283	        }
   284	        self.target_attempt(table_name, |runner| {
   285	            runner.upsert_attempt(table_name, key, row)
   286	        })
   287	    }
   288	
   289	    fn upsert_attempt(&mut self, table_name: &str, key: &Value, row: Supplied) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   290	        self.refuse_upsert_owned(table_name)?;
   291	        self.refuse_receipt_fields(table_name, &row, false)?;
   292	        self.refuse_recorded(table_name, &row)?;
   293	        super::sequences::refuse_fields(&self.schema.tables[table_name], table_name, &row)?;
   294	        let id = key.as_str()?;
   295	        if row.field("id")?.as_str()? != id {
   296	            return Err(RuntimeError::Input(format!("{table_name} upsert row id must equal its key")));
   297	        }
   298	        self.reserve_target_resolution(table_name, self.schema.table(table_name).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Schema(format!("missing table {table_name}")))?, &row, true)?;
   299	        match self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| {
   300	            runner.fetch_write_target(allowance, table_name, id)
   301	        })? {
   302	            Some(old) => {
   303	                let readable = !self.inactive_write_target(table_name, &old)?
   304	                    && self.check_rule(table_name, Effect::Read, None, &old)?;
   305	                let row = self.ignore_hidden_immutable_patch(table_name, row, readable)?;
   306	                // @ref LLP 3000.007#5.4 — an existing row receives a patch; omitted columns keep their values.
   307	                let (new, copy) = self.merge_patch(table_name, &old, &row, readable)?;
   308	                self.replace(table_name, old, new, readable, &row, copy)
   309	            }
   310	            None if self.device && !self.upsert_absence_proven(table_name, "byId", &[key.clone()])? =>
   311	            {
   312	                Err(self.write_miss(table_name, "byId", &[key.clone()]))
   313	            }
   314	            None => self.insert_upsert(table_name, "byId", row),
   315	        }
   316	    }
   317	
   318	    pub(super) fn insert_upsert(&mut self, table_name: &str, addressed_index: &str, row: Supplied) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   319	        self.refuse_upsert_owned(table_name)?;
   320	        // @ref LLP 3000.036.002#5 — trusted fixture imports preserve the constraint layer.
   321	        if self.context.is_system() {
   322	            return self.insert_attempt(table_name, row, false, Some(addressed_index)).map(|_| ()).map_err(|error| match error {
   323	                RuntimeError::Input(message) => RuntimeError::Constraint(message),
   324	                other => other,
   325	            });
   326	        }
   327	        if self.schema.tables[table_name].through.is_some() {
   328	            // A read-through child's insert arm keeps the hidden-target word for every authority refusal.
   329	            return self.insert_attempt(table_name, row, false, Some(addressed_index)).map(|_| ()).map_err(|e| match e {
   330	                RuntimeError::Rule {..} | RuntimeError::Input(_) => self.no_write_target(), other => other,
   331	            });
   332	        }
   333	        match self.insert_attempt(table_name, row, false, Some(addressed_index)).map(|_| ()) {
   334	            Err(RuntimeError::Input(_)) => Err(self.no_write_target()),
   335	            result => result,
   336	        }
   337	    }
   338	
   339	    fn replace(&mut self, table_name: &str, old: Value, new: Value, readable: bool, patch: &Value, copy: u64) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   340	        self.authorize_update_fields(table_name, &old, &new, patch, readable)?;
   341	        self.replace_authorized(table_name, old, new, readable, patch, copy)
   342	    }
   343	
   344	    /// `copy` is the merged image's lawful price, charged again for an engine slot copy.
   345	    pub(super) fn replace_authorized(&mut self, table_name: &str, old: Value, new: Value, readable: bool, patch: &Value, copy: u64) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   346	        self.refuse_engine_owned(table_name, Effect::Update)?;
   347	        self.refuse_receipt_fields(table_name, patch, false)?;
   348	        self.refuse_recorded(table_name, patch)?;
   349	        super::sequences::refuse_fields(&self.schema.tables[table_name], table_name, patch)?;
   350	        self.authorize_fields(table_name, &old, patch)?;
   351	        let definition = &self.schema.tables[table_name];
   352	        for path in definition.columns.keys().filter(|field| {
   353	            definition.engine_field(field) && field.as_str() != crate::schema::through::DEADLINE
   354	        }) {
   355	            if old.field(path).ok() != new.field(path).ok() {
   356	                return Err(if readable { RuntimeError::Structural { code: "E_RECORDED_FIELD", message: format!("engine replacement changed stored attribution at {table_name}.{path} (guide maintains)") } } else { self.no_write_target() });
   357	            }
   358	        }
   359	        let mut new = new;
   360	        self.schema.tables[table_name].recompute_deadline(&mut new)?;
   361	        // @ref LLP 3000.017#2.2 — extending life re-admits the new image.
   362	        if self.schema.tables[table_name].stamp_ephemeral(&mut new, self.context.now.unwrap_or(0))?
   363	            && !self.check_rule(table_name, Effect::Insert, None, &new)? {
   364	            return Err(if readable { RuntimeError::Rule { table: table_name.into(), effect: Effect::Update } } else { self.no_write_target() });
   365	        }
   366	        let new = self.with_asset_facts(table_name, new, Some(&old), (!readable).then_some(patch))?;
   367	        if let Err(error) = super::validate::validate_projection(self.schema, table_name, &new, self.device.then_some(self.context.viewer.as_str())) { return Err(if readable { error } else { self.no_write_target() }); }
   368	        self.check_constraints(table_name, Some(&old), &new, Effect::Update)?;
   369	        let new = self.prepare_event_slots(table_name, Some(&old), new, copy)?;
   370	        // A predicting device keeps another owner's omitted private field as an omission.
   371	        super::validate::validate_projection(self.schema, table_name, &new, self.device.then_some(self.context.viewer.as_str()))?;
   372	        let table = self.schema.table(table_name).expect("validated");
   373	        let entries = self.maintain_scratch(self.contribution_heap(table), |runner| {
   374	            runner.tx.put(table_name, table, &new, Some(&old))
   375	        })?;
   376	        self.charge_source_indexes(table, Some(&old), Some(&new), entries)?;
   377	        self.row_changed(table_name, Some(&old), Some(&new), Origin::Source)
   378	    }
   379	
   380	    pub(super) fn delete(&mut self, table_name: &str, id: &str) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   381	        if self.device && self.schema.tables[table_name].not_before.is_some() {
   382	            return Err(RuntimeError::Prediction(
   383	                "a mutation touching a `not before` table runs on the server".into(),
   384	            ));
   385	        }
   386	        self.target_attempt(table_name, |runner| runner.delete_attempt(table_name, id))
   387	    }
   388	
   389	    fn delete_attempt(&mut self, table_name: &str, id: &str) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   390	        self.refuse_engine_owned(table_name, Effect::Delete)?;
   391	        self.refuse_receipt_scope_delete(table_name)?;
   392	        let table = self.schema.table(table_name).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Schema(format!("missing table {table_name}")))?;
   393	        self.reserve_write_rules(table, &[Effect::Read, Effect::Delete])?;
   394	        // @ref LLP 3000.007#20.9 — delete prepays hidden contribution work before fetching its old image, with the same attempt lifetime as update.
   395	        self.reserve_maintains(table_name, table)?;
   396	        let Some(old) = self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| {
   397	            runner.fetch_write_target(allowance, table_name, id)
   398	        })? else {
   399	            return Err(RuntimeError::Require { site: Some(self.statement_site.clone()), code: "NOT_FOUND".to_owned(), message: None });
   400	        };
   401	        // @ref LLP 3000.039#3 — a delete that consults referencing rows needs read authority on its row first.
   402	        let readable =
   403	            !self.inactive_write_target(table_name, &old)? && self.check_rule(table_name, Effect::Read, None, &old)?;
   404	        if (self.schema.children(table_name).next().is_some() || self.schema.is_referenced(table_name)) && !readable
   405	        {
   406	            self.refusing_clause(table_name, "read rule");
   407	            return Err(self.no_write_target());
   408	        }
   409	        if !self.check_rule(table_name, Effect::Delete, None, &old)? {
   410	            return Err(if readable {
   411	                RuntimeError::Rule { table: table_name.to_owned(), effect: Effect::Delete }
   412	            } else { self.no_write_target() });
   413	        }
   414	        self.delete_authorized(table_name, old)
   415	    }
   416	
   417	    pub(super) fn delete_authorized(&mut self, table_name: &str, old: Value) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   418	        let old = if self.schema.is_referenced(table_name) {
   419	            self.apply_reference_actions(table_name, &old)?;
   420	            // @ref LLP 3000.039#3 — the actions may have changed the root (a maintained column mirrored from its children): remove its current image.
   421	            let id = old.field("id")?.as_str()?.to_owned();
   422	            self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.get(allowance, table_name, &id))?.unwrap_or(old)
   423	        } else { old };
   424	        self.delete_row(table_name, old)
   425	    }
   426	
   427	    /// A delete's own removal of one row, its rules already decided: receipt
   428	    /// membership, the read-through child probe, constraints, maintains and

   557	    pub(super) fn refuse_engine_owned(&self, table: &str, effect: Effect) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {

    60	    // Cache ordinary group keys once per target/query. Predicates and receipt
    61	    // fields are never evaluated; unknown/computed keys conservatively freeze
    62	    // the target. An unpinned read is incomplete if any group is dirty, while
    63	    // each returned row still decides independently whether to recount.
    64	    #[inline(never)]
    65	    pub(super) fn receipt_maintain_pending(&mut self, m: &Maintain, group: Option<&[Value]>) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {
    66	        if !self.defer_receipt_maintain(m) { return Ok(false); }
    67	        if !self.receipt_pending_groups.contains_key(&m.target) {
    68	            let fields = if let Some(k) = &m.row_key { vec![k.source_key.clone()] }
    69	                else { m.by.iter().map(|f| m.aliases.get(f).unwrap_or(f).clone()).collect() };
    70	            let mut groups = self.receipt_overlay_groups(&m.source, &fields, !m.computed.is_empty())?;
    71	            if let Some(k) = &m.row_key {
    72	                let member = self.receipt_overlay_groups(&k.table, std::slice::from_ref(&k.member_key), false)?;
    73	                groups = groups.zip(member).map(|(mut source, member)| { source.extend(member); source });
    74	            }
    75	            self.receipt_pending_groups.insert(m.target.clone(), groups);
    76	        }
    77	        let dirty = self.receipt_pending_groups[&m.target].as_ref().is_none_or(|keys|
    78	            group.map_or(!keys.is_empty(), |group| keys.iter().any(|key| key == group)));
    79	        if dirty {
    80	            self.value_source_incomplete = true;
    81	            self.components.note(|frame| frame.pending = true);
    82	        }
    83	        Ok(dirty)
    84	    }

    86	    fn receipt_overlay_groups(&self, table: &str, fields: &[String], computed: bool) -> Result<Option<Vec<Vec<Value>>>, RuntimeError> {
    87	        if !self.tx.has_provisional(table)? { return Ok(Some(Vec::new())); }
    88	        if computed || fields.iter().any(|f| self.schema.receipt_dependencies.get(table).is_some_and(|owned| owned.contains(f))) {
    89	            return Ok(None);

    94	    // Recover a read's parent/group from the pinned index. A member point uses
    95	    // one ordinary-key lookup; a scan without the parent stays conservative.
    96	    pub(super) fn receipt_read_group(&mut self, m: &Maintain, index: &str, key: &[Value]) -> Result<Option<Vec<Value>>, RuntimeError> {
    97	        if !self.defer_receipt_maintain(m) { return Ok(None); }
    98	        let columns = self.schema.tables[&m.target].indexes[index].columns();
    99	        let pinned = |field: &str| columns.iter().position(|c| c == field).and_then(|i| key.get(i)).cloned();

   111	    pub(super) fn maintain(&mut self, source: &str, old: Option<&Value>, new: Option<&Value>) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   112	        self.receipt_pending_groups.clear();
   113	        // Inserts ordinarily charge their actual aggregate work. A deferred
   114	        // predicate cannot select that work on a device, so use the same public
   115	        // worst-case reservation as update/delete before skipping it. Already
   116	        // prepaid writes must not pay twice.
   117	        if self.device && !self.maintain_prepaid && self.schema.maintains.iter().any(|m|
   118	            m.source == source && m.private.is_none() && m.row_key.is_none() && (self.schema.receipt_dependencies.contains_key(&m.target) || self.schema.tables[&m.target].sync.is_none())) {
   119	            self.reserve_maintains(source, &self.schema.tables[source])?;
   120	        }
   121	        self.maintain_row_views(source, old, new)?;
   122	        let maintains = self.schema.maintains.iter().filter(|maintain| maintain.source == source && maintain.row_key.is_none());
   123	        for maintain in maintains {
   124	            if self.defer_receipt_maintain(maintain) || (self.device && self.schema.tables[&maintain.target].sync.is_none()) { continue; }
   125	            let source_bytes = super::write_target::row_copy_ceiling(&self.schema.tables[&maintain.source]);
   126	            let target = &self.schema.tables[&maintain.target];
   127	            let bytes = source_bytes.saturating_mul(2).saturating_add(super::write_target::row_copy_ceiling(target).saturating_mul(16 + 4 * target.indexes.len() as u64));
   128	            let prepaid = self.maintain_prepaid;
   129	            if maintain.private.is_some() && self.column_prepaid { self.maintain_prepaid = true; }
   130	            let result = self.maintain_scratch(bytes, |runner| runner.maintain_one(maintain, old, new));
   131	            self.maintain_prepaid = prepaid;
   132	            result?;
   133	        }
   134	        Ok(())
   135	    }

   137	    // @ref LLP 3000.007#20.9 — reserve interpreted images, both keys, targets and index buffers before allocation; release transient ownership on every exit.
   138	    pub(super) fn maintain_scratch<T>(&mut self, bytes: u64, work: impl FnOnce(&mut Self) -> Result<T, RuntimeError>) -> Result<T, RuntimeError> {
   139	        if self.maintain_prepaid { return work(self); }
   140	        self.meter.heap(bytes)?;
   141	        let result = work(self);

   146	    fn maintain_one(&mut self, maintain: &Maintain, old: Option<&Value>, new: Option<&Value>) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   147	        let table = self.schema.table(&maintain.source).expect("validated");
   148	        let mut changes: Vec<(Vec<Value>, i128)> = Vec::new();
   149	        for (image, direction) in [(old, -1), (new, 1)] {
   150	            let Some(image) = image else { continue };
   151	            self.charge_maintain(MeterKind::Steps, maintain.evaluation_steps())?;
   152	            let image = crate::schema::row_image(image, table);
   153	            if !maintain.selected(&image) { continue; }
   154	            let key = maintain.source_key(&image);
   155	            let change = delta(maintain, &image, direction)?;
   156	            if let Some(existing) = changes.iter_mut().find(|(k, _)| *k == key) { existing.1 += change; }
   157	            else { changes.push((key, change)); }
   158	        }
   159	        for (key, change) in changes {
   160	            #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
   161	            if let Some(retiring) = self.retiring.as_mut() {
   162	                let entry = retiring.aggregates.entry((maintain.target.clone(), canonical_json(&key))).or_insert_with(|| (key, 0));
   163	                entry.1 = entry.1.checked_add(change).ok_or_else(|| aggregate_overflow(maintain))?;
   164	                continue;
   165	            }
   166	            if change != 0 || self.live_sum(maintain) {
   167	                self.apply_aggregate(maintain, key, change, None)?;
   168	            }
   169	        }
   170	        Ok(())
   171	    }
